title: auth_aka Module
content_markdown:
This module contains functions that are used to perform digest authentication using the AKA (Authentication and Key Agreement) security protocol. This mechanism is being used in IMS networks to provide mutual authentication between the UE (device) and the 3G/4G/5G network.

The AKA protocol establishes a set of security keys, called authentication vectors (or AVs), and uses them to generate the digest challenge, as well as for computing the digest result and authenticating the UE. AVs are exchanged over a separate communication channel.

Although the AKA protocol also requires to use the AVs to establish a secure channel between the UE and the network (by means of IPSec tunnels), this module does not handle that part - it just performs the authentication of the user and passes along the cyphering and integrity keys in the Authorization header, according to the _ETSI TS 129 229_ specifications. These are later on picked up by other components (such as P-CSCFs) to establish the secure channel.
overview:
This module contains functions that are used to perform digest authentication using the AKA (Authentication and Key Agreement) security protocol. This mechanism is being used in IMS networks to provide mutual authentication between the UE (device) and the 3G/4G/5G network.

The AKA protocol establishes a set of security keys, called authentication vectors (or AVs), and uses them to generate the digest challenge, as well as for computing the digest result and authenticating the UE. AVs are exchanged over a separate communication channel.

Although the AKA protocol also requires to use the AVs to establish a secure channel between the UE and the network (by means of IPSec tunnels), this module does not handle that part - it just performs the authentication of the user and passes along the cyphering and integrity keys in the Authorization header, according to the _ETSI TS 129 229_ specifications. These are later on picked up by other components (such as P-CSCFs) to establish the secure channel.
how_it_works:
Authentication Vectors (or AVs) consist of a set of five parameter (RAND, AUTN, XRES, CK, IK) that are being used for mutual authentication. As these need to be exchanged between the device (UE) and network through a different channel (i.e. Diameter Cx interface in LTE networks), the module does not provide any means to fetch the AV information. It does, however, provide a generic interface (called AV Manage Interface) to store AVs (that are being fetched by other modules/channels), manage them and use them in the digest authentication algorithm.

Basic AV operations that the module performs:

*   Ask for a new AV to be fetched for a specific user identity
    
*   Manage an AV lifetime, including reuses
    
*   Mark an AV as being used in a digest challeng
    
*   Invalidate or discard an AV (due to various reasons)
    

A module that implements the AV Manage Interface (called AV Manager) should be able to fetch all five parameters of an AV, and push them in the AV Storage.

The current implementation only supports the AKAv1 algorithms, with the associated hashing functions (such as MD5, SHA-256). In the challenge message, we send, one can advertise other algorithms as well, but the response cannot be handled by this module, and an appropriate error will be returned.

dependencies_required.name: AV manage module
dependencies_required.reason: at least one module that fetches AVs and pushes them in the AV storage

exported_parameters.name: default_av_mgm
exported_parameters.description: The default AV Manager used in case the functions do not provide them explicitly.
exported_parameters.example_code: modparam("auth\_aka", "default\_av\_mgm", "diameter") # fetch AVs through the Cx interface

exported_parameters.name: default_qop
exported_parameters.description: The default qop parameter used during challenge, if the functions do not provide them explicitly.

exported_parameters.name: default_algorithm
exported_parameters.description: The default algorithm to be advertise during challenge, if the functions do not provide them explicitly. _Note_ that at least one of the algorithms provided should be an AKA one, otherwise it makes no sense to use this module.
exported_parameters.notes: _WARNING:_ only AKAv1* algorithms are currently supported.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash that stores the AVs for each user. Must be a power of 2 number.

exported_parameters.name: sync_timeout
exported_parameters.description: The amount of milliseconds a synchronous call should wait for getting an authentication vector.
exported_parameters.notes: Must be a positive value. A value of _0_ indicates to wait indefinitely.

exported_parameters.name: async_timeout
exported_parameters.description: The amount of milliseconds an asynchronous call should wait for getting an authentication vector.
exported_parameters.notes: Must be a positive value, greater than 0. _NOTE:_ the current timeout mechanism only has seconds granularity, therefore you should configure this parameter as a multiple of 1000.

exported_parameters.name: unused_timeout
exported_parameters.description: The amount of seconds an authentication vector that has not been used can stay in memory. Once this timeout is reached, the authentication vector is removed.
exported_parameters.notes: Must be a positive value, greater than 0.

exported_parameters.name: pending_timeout
exported_parameters.description: The amount of seconds an authentication vector that is being used in the authentication process shall stay in memory. Once this timeout is reached, the authentication vector is removed, and the authentication using it will fail.
exported_parameters.notes: Must be a positive value, greater than 0.

exported_functions.name: aka_www_authorize

parameters.name: realm
parameters.default: host part of From header field URI
parameters.description: Realm is a opaque string that the user agent should present to the user so he can decide what username and password to use. This is usually one of the domains the proxy is responsible for.

return_values.condition: sync request (the auts parameter was present, thus a sync was requested)
generic error (some generic error occurred and no reply was sent out)
no credentials (credentials were not found in request)
unknown nonce (authentication vector with the corresponding nonce was not found)
invalid password (password does not match the authentication vector)
invalid username (no username found in the Authorize header)
success (credentials verified successfully)

exported_functions.description: The function verifies credentials according to RFC3310, by using an authentication vector priorly allocated by an `aka_www_challenge()` call, using the _av_mgm_ manager. If the credentials are verified successfully the function will succeed, otherwise it will fail with an appropriate error code. In case the function succeeds, the _WWW-Authenticate_ header is being added to the reply, containing the challenge information, as well as the _Integrity-Key_ and the _Confidentiality-Key_ values associated to the AV being used. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions).

exported_functions.name: aka_proxy_authorize

parameters.name: realm
parameters.default: host part of From header field URI
parameters.description: Realm is a opaque string that the user agent should present to the user so he can decide what username and password to use. This is usually one of the domains the proxy is responsible for.

return_values.condition: sync request
generic error
no credentials
unknown nonce
invalid password
invalid username
success

exported_functions.description: The function behaves the same as `aka_www_authorize()`, but it authenticates the user from a proxy perspective. It receives the same parameters, with the same meaning, and returns the same values.

exported_functions.name: aka_www_challenge

parameters.name: av_mgm
parameters.description: The AV Manager to be used for this challenge, in case an AV is not already available for the challenged user identity.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Realm is an opaque string that the user agent should present to the user so it can decide what username and password to use. Usually this is domain of the host the server is running on.

parameters.name: qop
parameters.description: Value of this parameter can be either “auth”, “auth-int” or both (separated by _,_). When this parameter is set the server will put a qop parameter in the challenge.

parameters.name: algorithms
parameters.description: Value of this parameter is a comma-separated list of digest algorithms to be offered for the UAC to use for authentication.

return_values.condition: generic parsing error (not enough data to build the challenge)
no AV vector could be fetched
authentication headers could not be built
a reply could not be sent
the number of successful challenges being sent in the reply

exported_functions.description: The function challenges a user agent. It fetches an authentication vector for each algorigthm used through the _av_mgm_ Manager and generate one or more WWW-Authenticate header fields containing digest challenges. It will put the header field(s) into a response generated from the request the server is processing and will send the reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials using the used authentication vector annd retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617, RFC3261, RFC3310 and RFC8760.

parameters.name: av_mgm
parameters.description: The AV Manager to be used for this challenge, in case an AV is not already available for the challenged user identity.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Realm is an opaque string that the user agent should present to the user so it can decide what username and password to use. Usually this is domain of the host the server is running on.

parameters.name: qop
parameters.description: Value of this parameter can be either “auth”, “auth-int” or both (separated by _,_). When this parameter is set the server will put a qop parameter in the challenge.

parameters.name: algorithms
parameters.description: Value of this parameter is a comma-separated list of digest algorithms to be offered for the UAC to use for authentication.

return_values.condition: generic parsing error
no AV vector could be fetched
authentication headers could not be built
a reply could not be sent
the number of successful challenges being sent in the reply

exported_functions.description: The function behaves the same as `aka_www_challenge()`, but it challenges the user from a proxy perspective. It receives the same parameters, with the same meaning, the only difference being that in case of the _realm_ is missing, then it is taken from the the _To domain_, rather than from _From domain_. The header added is _Proxy-Authenticate_, rather than _WWW-Authenticate_ The rest of the parameters, behavior, as well as return values are the same.

exported_functions.name: aka_av_add
exported_functions.signature: aka_av_add(public_identity, private_identity, authenticate, authorize, confidentiality_key, integrity_key[, algorithms])

parameters.name: public_identity
parameters.description: The public identity (IMPU) of the user to add authentication vector for.

parameters.name: private_identity
parameters.description: The private identity (IMPI) of the user to add authentication vector for.

parameters.name: authenticate
parameters.description: The concatenation of the authentication challenge RAND and the token AUTN, encoded in hexa format.

parameters.name: authorize
parameters.description: The authorization string (XRES) used for authorizing the user, encoded in hexa format.

parameters.name: confidentiality_key
parameters.description: The Confidentiality-Key used in the AKA IPSec process, encoded in hexa format.

parameters.name: integrity_key
parameters.description: The Integrity-Key used in the AKA IPSec process, encoded in hexa format.

parameters.name: algorithms
parameters.description: AKA algorithms this AV should be used for. If missing, the AV can be used for any AKA algorithm.

exported_functions.description: Adds an authentication vector for the user identitied by _public_identity_ and _private_identity_.

exported_functions.name: aka_av_drop

parameters.name: public_identity
parameters.description: The public identity (IMPU) of the user to drop authentication vector for.

parameters.name: private_identity
parameters.description: The private identity (IMPI) of the user to drop authentication vector for.

parameters.name: authenticate
parameters.description: The authenticate/nonce that identifies the authentication vector to be dropped.

exported_functions.description: Drops the authentication vector corresponding to the _authenticate/nonce_ value for an user identitied by _public_identity_ and _private_identity_.

exported_functions.name: aka_av_drop_all

parameters.name: public_identity
parameters.description: The public identity (IMPU) of the user to drop authentication vectors for.

parameters.name: private_identity
parameters.description: The private identity (IMPI) of the user to drop authentication vectors for.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: A variable to return the number of authentication vectors dropped.

exported_functions.description: Drops all authentication vectors for an user identitied by _public_identity_ and _private_identity_. This function is useful when a synchronization must be done.

exported_functions.name: aka_av_fail

parameters.name: public_identity
parameters.description: The public identity (IMPU) of the user to drop authentication vectors for.

parameters.name: private_identity
parameters.description: The private identity (IMPI) of the user to drop authentication vectors for.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of authentication vectors that failed.

exported_functions.description: Marks the engine that an authentication vector query for a user has failed, unlocking the processing of the message. _Note:_ this function is useful when you know that fetching a new authentication vector is not possible (due to various reasons) - calling it will resume the message procesing, using only the available AVs fetched so far.

exported_mi_functions.description: Adds an Authentication Vector through the MI interface.

examples.code:
## adds an AKA AV
$ opensips-cli -x mi aka\_av\_add \\
					sip:test@siphub.com
					test@siphub.com
					KFQ/MpR3cE3V9PxucEQS5KED8uUNYIAALFyk59sIJI4=
					00000262c0000014000028af2d6398cbe26eea69
					db7f8c4a58e17083974bba3b936d34c4
					6151667b9ef815c1dcb87473685f062a
